correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the bijection F=E(G[V\W]), nonwhite positive selected degree and selected-degree-one neighbours of every white vertex. For ordinary degree-two paths the forbidden pairs of white positions have distance at most two; terminal constraints and the degree-(r+2) root are all handled explicitly. The four root cases are exhaustive, disjoint and sufficient. Forced-endpoint path-word counts give the exact coefficients; 468 independent edge-subset enumerations and a larger special-family replay confirm but do not prove the infinite claim.

value.rationale: Natural arbitrary-armed unicyclic graphs provide a flexible exact counting benchmark within a generally hard enumeration problem. The formula counts every PED-set and identifies the four possible root configurations. Holding cycle length fixed, one-edge arms yield affine dependence on arm count, whereas two-edge arms yield exact 2^r exponential growth after one subdivision per arm. The 3-parameter and arbitrary-vector structure is not a routine numeric update of the prior r=1 formula.
